name: Ursa Major and Canes Venatici
description: Containing several nearby stars, Ursa Major is distorted quite badly. ξ Ursae Majoris is pushed out of the constellation, and Pollux (seen in Gemini from Earth) makes an appearance. α Canum Venaticorum is a naked-eye double.

name: Orion
description: Orion consists mostly of distant stars, so its shape is largely intact (here shown upside-down, since Erid's north-south axis is roughly antiparallel Earth's). Only χ<sup>1</sup> Orionis and π<sup>3</sup> Orionis are close enough to be shifted out of the constellation.

name: Octans and Chamaeleon
description: Octans and Chamaeleon contain no bright stars, so this region of sky appears nearly empty — though α Trianguli Australis is on the border of this region. Erid has no easily visible north pole star.

name: Ursa Minor
description: Ursa Minor fares even worse than its larger sibling. The familiar shape of the "dipper" is nowhere to be seen, and the constellation is not circumpolar.

name: Canis Major
description: Though most of the individual stars of Canis Major are distant, its brightest star, Sirius, is rather close to Sol. You could still draw a dog with the visible stars, in a different orientation from Earth's.
